newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: AMMB plans two rights issues.
newsitem.headline: AMMB plans two rights issues.

text.p: AMMB Holdings Bhd said on Tuesday that it plans two rights issues to raise between 865 million and 890 million ringgit which will enable the company to strengthen its capital base.
AMMB had said last week that it planned to make a cash call to help the expansion of its commercial banking arm.

In a statement, the financial services concern said it had proposed a rights issue of up to 445.25 million ringgit of loan stocks as well as a second rights issue of up to 445.25 million ringgit of bonds.
The loan stocks, or bonds convertible into stocks, are due in 2002 with interest at the rate of 7.5 percent a year.
The bonds are also due in 2002 with an interest rate of 5.0 percent per annum. Every 10 ringgit nominal amount of the bonds will be issued with one warrant due in the year 2002.

AMMB said that 250 million ringgit from the proceeds would be used to increase the capital base of Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd and 300 million ringgit to boost the capital base of Arab-Malaysian Bank Bhd.

Of the proceeds, another 300 million ringgit would be used towards the proposed subscription of AMMB Holdings' entitlement to Arab-Malaysian Finance Bhd's proposed 481.4 million ringgit loan stock rights issue.
In a separate announcement on Tuesday, Arab-Malaysian Finance said it planned a one-for-one rights issue of loan stocks with an interest rate of 7.5 percent and a five-year tenure.
Arab-Malaysia Finance also said it planned a one-for-one bonus issue of up to 240.70 million new ordinary shares.
Both the rights and bonus issues will strengthen the company's capital base, Arab-Malaysian Finance said.
